title: Shaah Cadays
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Somalia's beloved spiced milk tea, black tea simmered with cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves until deeply fragrant, then sweetened generously and served throughout the day as a gesture of hospitality.
longDesc: Shaah cadays is woven into the rhythm of daily Somali life, brewed fresh multiple times a day and always offered to guests as a first gesture of welcome, its warm spice blend reflecting the same Indian Ocean trade routes that shaped so much of Somali cuisine.
ingredients: 3 black tea bags or 3 tbsp loose black tea
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a saucepan with the cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves.
Reduce to a simmer and let the spices infuse for 5 minutes.
Add the tea and simmer for another 3-4 minutes until deeply colored.
Add the milk and sugar, and bring back to a gentle simmer, stirring.
Simmer for another 2-3 minutes until well combined and fragrant.
Strain into cups and serve hot.
chefTips: Simmering the whole spices in water first, before adding the tea, allows their flavor to fully infuse.
Adjust the sugar to taste - Somali tea is traditionally served quite sweet.
This tea is a genuine gesture of hospitality - always offered warmly to guests.
commonMistakes: Adding the milk too early, before the spices have had a chance to properly infuse the water.
Boiling too vigorously once the milk is added, which can cause it to curdle or scorch.
Using pre-ground spices instead of whole ones, which provide a less aromatic result.
storage: Best made fresh; does not keep well once prepared.
reheating: Reheat gently on the stovetop, taking care not to boil.
healthBenefits: Cardamom and cinnamon offer some antioxidant properties; best enjoyed with moderate sugar.
culturalNote: Shaah cadays is a fundamental part of Somali hospitality, traditionally the first thing offered to any guest entering a home, brewed fresh multiple times throughout the day.
